pictures.scene: Jean-Leon Gerome, The Plain of Thebes during the Flooding of the Nile - the two great seated colossi standing up out of the still flood water at dusk with their own reflections lying under them, the flamingos and the storks wading in the pale shallows at the left and a thin line of birds going over, the long misty mountain ridge and the orange and violet sky behind them, then Israel entered Egypt Jacob dwelt in the land of Ham, and the LORD made His people very fruitful more numerous than their foes
pictures.name: pd_gerome_memnonkolossen

pictures.scene: Jean-Paul Laurens, Saint John Chrysostom and the Empress Eudoxia - the empress standing in her gold embroidered gown in the gallery at the left with her crowned attendant behind her and the animal figured tapestry hung at her back, the bishop out at his pulpit on the right in his white robe with both arms thrown wide open as he speaks, the gold ochre wall and the mosaic arch standing over them, whose hearts He turned to hate His people, to conspire against His servants
pictures.name: pd_laurens_chrysostomus

pictures.scene: Alexander Heubel, Moses, Aaron and Hur - Moses standing in the middle in the white robe and the red mantle with the rays of light coming out of his head and his hands held up, the aged Aaron kneeling close at the left in green and gold with his face lifted to him, Hur standing steady at the right, the deep blue sky of the hilltop open behind the three of them, he sent Moses His servant and Aaron whom He had chosen, they performed His miraculous signs among them and wonders in the land of Ham
pictures.name: pd_heubel_mozes_aaron

pictures.scene: Abraham van Beijeren, Still Life with Fish - the dead fish heaped up in the wicker basket in the dark kitchen, the long silver ones laid across one another with their mouths open and their eyes gone dull, the cut side of the salmon turned out red and raw beside them, the mussels spilled down on the bare table with the knife and the green cloth, the whole back of the room sunk in brown shadow, he sent darkness and it became dark yet they defied His words, he turned their waters to blood and caused their fish to die, their land teemed with frogs even in their royal chambers
pictures.name: pd_beijeren_stilleven_met_vissen

pictures.scene: Francisque Millet, Mountain Landscape with Lightning - the single bolt coming straight down the middle of the picture out of the black cloud with the gold light breaking behind it, the rain hanging in a grey curtain over the valley and the far snow mountains lit along the top, the little walled town and the arch of the bridge down in the dark below, the woman on the bank at the bottom throwing her arm up at the sky and the man in blue sitting beside her, he spoke and insects swarmed gnats throughout their country, he gave them hail for rain with lightning throughout their land, he struck their vines and fig trees and shattered the trees of their country
pictures.name: pd_millet_berglandschap_met_bliksem

pictures.scene: Hans Andersen Brendekilde, Worn Out - the huge bare field of brown earth and loose flints running back empty to the horizon under a flat grey sky, the old labourer fallen flat on his back in the dirt with his arm thrown out and his cap knocked off beside his hand, the woman down on her knees over him in the red sleeves and the sack coloured shawl with her head turned away and her mouth open crying out for help, he spoke and the locusts came young locusts without number, they devoured every plant in their land and consumed the produce of their soil, then He struck all the firstborn in their land the firstfruits of all their vigor
pictures.name: pd_brendekilde_uitgeput

lines.text: Then Israel entered Egypt;
Jacob dwelt in the land of Ham.
And the LORD made His people very fruitful,
more numerous than their foes,
whose hearts He turned to hate His people,
to conspire against His servants.
He sent Moses His servant,
and Aaron, whom He had chosen.
They performed His miraculous signs among them,
and wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness, and it became dark—
yet they defied His words.
He turned their waters to blood
and caused their fish to die.
Their land teemed with frogs,
even in their royal chambers.
He spoke, and insects swarmed—
gnats throughout their country.
He gave them hail for rain,
with lightning throughout their land.
He struck their vines and fig trees
and shattered the trees of their country.
He spoke, and the locusts came—
young locusts without number.
They devoured every plant in their land
and consumed the produce of their soil.
Then He struck all the firstborn in their land,
the firstfruits of all their vigor.
